layer.platform: what every app runs on: cluster policy, operators, shared services, cloud accounts, identity, networking, and the templates apps use to get them.
layer.app: software that does work people use, and its data, agents and jobs (Hermes, gbrain, Hindsight, collectors, agent harnesses).

target.cluster: lands in the Kubernetes cluster, including manifests and configuration for hosting storage, processing and agents, and changing the working version of a Helm release (usually a pin change).
target.cloud: lands at a cloud provider (Cloudflare, Google).
target.image: changes a public Helm chart or its image.
target.none: design, planning or coordination, or work a person wants to steer in their own thread.

domain: App code is code. It is built into a container image and shipped with a Helm chart. Images and charts live in oci.
The GitOps repos (basis, cloud-basis, brain) hold manifests and configuration only, deployed by Flux as written. They never hold app code.

brain holds app manifests, builder pod releases and their values, and the configuration of agent environments: the harness layers (settings, hooks, skills, prompts, and small glue such as a bash alias that blocks sed).
basis holds the platform every app runs on inside the cluster, including shared platform services (the flux MCP, the logs API and logs MCP, alerting, cluster health checks).

cloud-basis owns Crossplane and its Cloudflare and GCP providers (even though they run in the cluster), every Cloudflare, Google Workspace and GCP account-level resource (zones, tunnels, Zero Trust, projects), and Kyverno policies that generate cloud resources. Questions about these are cloud-basis work, except one app's own DNS record or access policy, which stays with that app in brain.
oci builds and owns these products: builder-sb, cred-rotator, cluster, gbrain, agentdb. Each product's own code, image and Helm chart are oci work, including what the product does at runtime.
projects plans and coordinates, and writes Efforts. It changes no repo.

Moving a pinned version in the cluster is a pin change in brain: a builder release (build-basis, build-cloud-basis, build-brain, build-oci, build-projects, also with an ssint- prefix) to another chart version, or an app pin such as gbrain, hermes-agent or hindsight to another release.
Harness layers (builder, project, desktop) are brain's agent configuration. Building, publishing or changing a harness layer is layer app, target cluster.

agents.basis: the cluster-wide base stack: operator installs (cert-manager, Kyverno, CloudNativePG, observability), Kyverno cluster and cleanup policies, and platform services shared by every namespace (the flux MCP, the logs API and logs MCP, alerting, cluster health checks).
agents.cloud-basis: Crossplane and its Cloudflare and GCP providers; Cloudflare resources (DNS, tunnels, Access apps and policies, Workers, Zero Trust); Google Workspace and GCP resources; the cluster MCP connector's routes into the cluster; Kyverno policies that generate Crossplane resources.
agents.brain: all app code, manifests and configuration for hosting storage, processing and agents in the cluster: Hermes, gbrain, Hindsight, Big AGI, collectors and ingest jobs, model config; builder pod releases and their values (chart pins, MCP config); builder policy published as harness layers (managed settings, hooks, skills, agent prompts); the Effort MCP and other app services in the ssint namespaces; image and chart pins for gbrain, hermes-agent and hindsight.
agents.oci: building and publishing container images (builder-sb, cred-rotator, cluster, gbrain, agentdb); the builder Helm chart and its releases; node bootstrap and kube-vip.
agents.projects: planning and coordinating cross-repo delivery; creating, splitting, updating and closing Efforts and their tasks; anything that fits no other agent.
